answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each identity’s ledger begins with a harbor of unspent compute credits earned only through verified task completion; clones start empty. To bridge into paid work, a new identity must complete a costly calibration task whose output is checked against a hidden reef of known-good results, so fake identities fail and forfeit the calibration cost. Attacker pays that compute plus lost calibration time per clone, while honest agents amortize one calibration across real earnings.
